benchmark.occupation_mapping_rule:
Map every 2019 dictionary OCCP code to one of the five official broad groups.

Source of the groups: the official '2018 American Community Survey PUMS Occupation Code List'
(sheet 'ACS'), whose header rows list the five civilian broad groups with their code ranges and whose
body lists every code under its group. The mapping is taken from that document, code by code:
each individual 4-digit code row inherits the most recent broad-group header row above it.
Cross-check: the 2019 dictionary label prefixes (MGR, BUS, ..., MIL) must be consistent with the groups.

predicate.duplicates: (SERIALNO, SPORDER) must be unique; any duplicate person key aborts extraction
predicate.employment: ESR in {"1","2"} (civilian employed, at work / with a job but not at work)
predicate.household_residents: SERIALNO matches ^2019HU[0-9]{7}$ (housing-unit person); every 2019GQ (group quarters) row excluded
predicate.inputs: AGEP, WKHP numeric as above; COW, SCHL, MAR, POBP non-blank strings (any other blank -> row ineligible and counted)
predicate.occupation: OCCP non-blank, present in the 2019 dictionary, and mapped to one of the five civilian groups (military 9800-9830, 9920 and blank excluded)

claim_rules.COMPETITIVE_COMPARISON: SUPERIOR_TO_ALL_ELIGIBLE (coalition recovery only) iff the comparison is complete, LOCAL_TREE meets the same utility requirements (the baselines' eligibility rule: 24-clause MODEL_SELECT point feasibility on both seeds; plus the DEV_REPORT 24-clause point gate of RECIPE_EFFECT), at least one required baseline is ELIGIBLE, and coalition benefit vs every ELIGIBLE required baseline (NEURAL_RAW, FAGTB two-task, FARE) has one-sided alpha/3 lower bound > 0 on both seeds; INCOMPLETE if a required family is missing or invalid (never a win); LOCAL_TREE_FAILS_SAME_UTILITY_REQUIREMENTS if the LOCAL_TREE gate fails; the decision names the eligible set; ineligible baselines and recipient-level differences are descriptive. Nested (no extra alpha): MATERIALLY_SUPERIOR_TO_ALL_ELIGIBLE at margin 0.020.
claim_rules.RECIPE_EFFECT: ESTABLISHED iff (IUT, one-sided alpha/3 per clause) coalition benefit vs TASK_REFIT has lower bound > 0.020 on both seeds AND each recipient worsening has upper bound <= 0.010 on both seeds, AND (point-feasibility gate; a deterministic condition on the estimates, no error control) all 24 LOCAL_TREE utility clauses pass at the point. Reported separately: the count of utility clauses whose one-sided alpha/3 upper bound <= cap, and the nested decision RECIPE_EFFECT_AND_UTILITY_BOUNDS (all 30 clauses at their bounds; same clause tests, no extra alpha). Conditional on the two fitted seed pairs and the frozen readers.
claim_rules.SUBGROUP_SUITABILITY: SUBGROUP_QUALIFIED iff all four guards (occupation summed-Brier excess vs U0 within each SEX group, both seeds) have one-sided alpha/3 upper bound <= 0.005 (IUT); ESTABLISHED_SUBGROUP_HARM iff any guard has K = 40 simultaneous lower bound > 0.005; otherwise SUBGROUP_UNRESOLVED (crossing intervals are unresolved, never harm); NOT_ESTIMABLE if fewer than 200 DEV_REPORT households contain a member of a SEX group (counted from SEX alone, before any outcome is computed). All PASS/VIOLATION/SHORTFALL/HARM labels are read from the K = 40 simultaneous intervals; marginal alpha/3 bounds decide only the positive claim clauses.

inference.design:
Open DEV_REPORT once (after the committed REPORTING_LOCK) and evaluate the frozen roster.

Inference (SCIENCE_LOCK 'inference'): one nonparametric household (cluster) bootstrap (B = 2048, seed 2026101603) over DEV_REPORT
households, shared across every service, endpoint and both fitted seeds (paired). Every bound is Wald-type: point +/- t(G - 1) x
bootstrap SE (G = DEV_REPORT households); this is not a studentized bootstrap-t.
Decision family (positive direction only): three claims, each an intersection-union test (IUT) whose bound-based clauses are tested at
one-sided level alpha/3 (alpha = 0.025; Bonferroni across the three claims). Hence P(at least one of the three positive claim decisions is
false) <= 0.025 ONE-SIDED (each claim <= 0.0083 one-sided), approximately (Wald clause tests), conditional on the fitted models and readers.
RECIPE_EFFECT = 6 bound-based clauses plus a 24-clause utility POINT-feasibility gate (a deterministic condition on the estimates, with no
error control); its nested decision that also requires the 24 utility clauses to pass at their alpha/3 bounds shares the clause tests
and needs no further alpha. COMPETITIVE_COMPARISON = coalition benefit > 0 vs every eligible required baseline, both seeds, gated by
LOCAL_TREE meeting the same utility requirements. SUBGROUP_SUITABILITY = four guards. The IUT is NOT a simultaneous coverage statement:
per-clause alpha/3 bounds are marginal and can neither establish violations, shortfalls or harm nor be counted after a failed conjunction.
Reporting family: two-sided 95% intervals over the frozen K = 40 primary roster (Bonferroni t), with approximate simultaneous coverage
conditional on the fitted models and readers; every failing-direction label (ESTABLISHED_VIOLATION, ESTABLISHED_SHORTFALL,
ESTABLISHED_SUBGROUP_HARM) is read from these simultaneous intervals only.
Scope: the two seeds share people and are not independent samples; each seed is its own clause, so 'both seeds' is a two-fit
replication, not an estimate of between-fit variance. The household bootstrap treats DEV_REPORT households as a simple random sample
from a household superpopulation (unweighted ACS-sample composition); it is not ACS survey-design variance (no strata, PUMA clustering
or PWGTP1-80 replicate weights). PWGTP-weighted values are point summaries only.
Pre-registered sensitivity (reported, never decisive): one-sided percentile bounds from the same draws and bootstrap skewness per
roster endpoint; every disagreement with the primary Wald decision is disclosed.
inference.familywise: decision family: one-sided FWER 0.025 over the three positive claim decisions (Bonferroni, alpha/3 = 0.0083 per claim; IUT within claims; Wald clause tests, approximate); reporting family: K = 40 two-sided simultaneous 95% intervals (approximate simultaneous coverage); the two families carry separate guarantees and are labelled separately
inference.scope: all intervals and decisions are conditional on the two fitted seed pairs and the frozen readers, in the unweighted DEV_REPORT household superpopulation; they do not quantify between-fit (training) variance or uncertainty about the recipe effect over refits
inference.sealed_assessment: remains closed; a favourable DEV_REPORT does not authorise opening it
inference.sensitivity: pre-registered: one-sided percentile bounds from the same 2,048 draws and bootstrap skewness for every roster endpoint; the primary Wald bound governs and every disagreement is disclosed
inference.separation: the three conclusions are reported separately and never merged; an UNQUALIFIED recommendation requires SUBGROUP_QUALIFIED; under SUBGROUP_UNRESOLVED any recommendation must state that subgroup suitability is unresolved; under ESTABLISHED_SUBGROUP_HARM (simultaneous intervals) no recommendation for that group; crossing intervals are unresolved, never established harm
inference.weighted_secondary: PWGTP-weighted point summaries (ratio estimators) of AUCs and utility, targeting the person-weighted Florida 2019 household-resident cohort analogue for the same fitted models; no interval is attached to weighted values; the household-bootstrap intervals apply only to the unweighted primary estimands; ACS design-based variance (PWGTP1-80 replicate weights, successive-difference replication) is not computed

T_TREE.headroom_gate:
Teacher headroom on MODEL_SELECT (both seeds) and the pre-registered usefulness gate.

Metrics per task and service (T_TREE, U0, Ucal): NLL, summed Brier, accuracy, gain over constant prediction
(accuracy, NLL, Brier), balanced accuracy, per-class recall. Headroom = U0 minus T_TREE (positive = teacher better).
Gate (SCIENCE_LOCK): the benchmark is SUPPORTED and the teacher USEFUL iff, for both tasks and both seeds, T_TREE has
positive NLL gain and positive accuracy gain over constant prediction on MODEL_SELECT and MODEL_FIT task-class support
passed. A useful teacher continues through the fixed protected recipe even if headroom over U0 is small or negative;
otherwise the study closes as UNSUPPORTED after this honest diagnostic comparison.
T_TREE.rule: internal fold early stopping: tree count = first argmin of internal loss + 1; refit on all MODEL_FIT with that count and seed; numpy teacher verified bitwise against CatBoost

U0.note: validated source per-task network with only input width and occupation output count changed; Recipe A on MODEL_FIT with a 15% household-disjoint internal fold, refit on all MODEL_FIT

spec.architecture: d-64-ReLU-64-ReLU-16-linear K (ACS-CHANGE: d = ACS input width)

Ucal.rule: one global positive temperature per task: T* = argmin_T mean NLL of softmax(centered U0 logits / T) on CALIBRATION

selection.rule:
Frozen MODEL_SELECT rule: one common configuration across both seeds for every tunable control.

Rule (SCIENCE_LOCK 'selection'): (1) task feasibility first: a configuration is FEASIBLE iff all 24 point utility
clauses (2 tasks x {U0, Ucal} x {accuracy loss <= 0.010, NLL excess <= 0.010, summed Brier excess <= 0.005} x 2 seeds)
pass on MODEL_SELECT; (2) among feasible configurations, minimise the mean over seeds of the validation recovery proxy:
coalition AUC on MODEL_SELECT of a fixed OUT_LR reader (LogisticRegression C=1 on the released pair wire, finite
scaler) trained on the MODEL_FIT pair wire with MODEL_FIT SEX; ties by the fixed grid order; (3) if no configuration
is feasible, freeze one diagnostic fallback minimising the maximum normalised clause value (value / cap) over all 24
clauses, ties by grid order; the fallback is INELIGIBLE (descriptive only). LOCAL_TREE (rho1 E20), TASK_REFIT (E20),
T_TREE and the references are fixed and reported, never selected. No DEV_REPORT, ATTACK or SEALED label is read.
